_doc: Dynamic security-advisory whitelist (Decision: dynamic whitelist, 2026-06-17). SINGLE SOURCE for scripts/audit-security.ts, and through it for .github/workflows/security-advisory-watch.yml — do not duplicate the list anywhere else. Until 2026-09-16 this line also named dependabot-labeler.yml as a reader. It never was one: the labeler keeps its own QUASAR_BLOCKED list, and converging the advisory surfaces is an open consolidation item (security-advisory-watch.yml header). Each entry is a PACKAGE whose high/critical advisories are ACKNOWLEDGED (not auto-failed) with a documented, dated reason. The auditor AUTO-DERIVES transitives: a vulnerable package whose every dependency path to root passes through an acknowledged package is acknowledged automatically (no entry needed) — so esbuild/ajv/minimatch/etc. need no explicit row. Auto-derivation is FAIL-CLOSED: if the auditor cannot prove every path runs through an acknowledged package, the advisory FAILS. A package that is independently fixable within its semver constraint must be FIXED, never whitelisted (fixing > acknowledging). Refresh/review with: npm run refresh:security-allowlist.

_categories.dev-test-only: Pulled only by a dev/test dependency — never present in the production runtime artifact.
_categories.build-time-only: Pulled only by the build toolchain (PWA/workbox/bundler) — runs at build time, not shipped in the bundle.
_categories.awaiting-upstream: Direct or near-direct dependency ALREADY at its latest published version; there is nothing to move to. Covers both “the advisory's fix is not published yet” and “no newer major exists” — the same state from the consumer's side. Re-check at reviewBy with `npm run refresh:security-allowlist`, and re-measure rather than re-reading the reason.
_categories.context-safe: The advisory's exploit precondition is not met by how the package is used here (e.g., a ReDoS that requires attacker-controlled input, where every call site receives only developer-controlled input). Must document the specific precondition per package.
_categories.peer-blocked:
A newer major exists but an INSTALLED peer constraint rejects it — and the blocker is named, because “a framework pins it” was assumed here for 11 entries and was true for none. `npm run check:peer-constraints -- --package

--candidate --check-upstream` names every blocker and reports STILL BLOCKS / WOULD ADMIT / UNKNOWN against the registry; UNKNOWN never folds into “still blocked”. Clear the entry when the trigger fires.

vue.reason: Already on the newest published major (3.5.41 = latest); there is no Vue 4 to move to. Re-measured 2026-08-23 against the registry. Previously filed as framework-pinned, which was never true — its own reason said “NOT blocked by Quasar”.

vue-router.reason: Already on the newest published major (5.2.0 = latest). @quasar/app-vite peers `^4.0.12 || ^5.0.0`, so v5 was admitted all along; nothing is held back. Re-measured 2026-08-23.

pinia.reason: Already on the newest published major (4.0.3 = latest). Re-measured 2026-08-23; the earlier reason described a pinia-3-vs-4 gate that no longer exists, and noted no advisory attaches to pinia at all.

@vitejs/plugin-vue.reason: Already on the newest published major (6.0.8 = latest). A real direct dep — vitest.config.ts imports it, and vitest sits outside Quasar's build chain. Re-measured 2026-08-23.

typescript.reason: Genuinely blocked, and NOT by a framework: typescript@7.0.2 is rejected by 8 of 15 installed peer constraints, every one of them `@typescript-eslint/*` capping at `<6.1.0`. Quasar peers `>= 5.4` and accepts 7 — asking Quasar alone is what produced the original false UNBLOCKED. Verify with: `npm run check:peer-constraints -- --package typescript --candidate 7.0.2 --check-upstream`. Re-measured 2026-08-23.

@vue/test-utils.reason: unit-test harness only (pulls js-beautify → js-cookie); never in the production runtime

@stryker-mutator/core.reason: mutation-testing tool only; never in the production runtime

vitest.reason: unit-test runner; never in the production runtime

typescript-eslint.reason: lint tooling (pulls minimatch via TS rules); never in the production runtime

workbox-build.reason: Quasar PWA service-worker build (pulls @babel/preset-env → transform plugins); runs at build time, not shipped in the bundle
